study: Stage 2 of the paid-data decision: does Nasdaq order-book depth (information the desk has never seen) predict short-term direction in the desk's names well enough to beat the spread?
registered_at: 2026-10-04, before any depth data was bought or fetched

data.source: Databento XNAS.ITCH (Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH), schema mbp-10 (top-10 price levels, aggregated size); historical, pay-as-you-go against the $125 new-account credit
data.budget_guard: before any download, price every request with Databento's metadata.get_cost; abort if the total exceeds $100. Nothing is downloaded outside the windows below.
data.key: the user's Databento API key in config/secrets.json.databento on the mini (gitignored); never printed or logged
data.signals: desk day-trade entries with entry_price >= $10 from ai_reports/outcomes.jsonl (hold_days 0, deduplicated), 2026-09-16 through the last session before the run, restricted to Nasdaq-listed symbols (Alpaca asset exchange == NASDAQ); signal time = entry_test.t_decide when present, else entry_time
data.random: 2 random entry minutes per desk signal, same name and day, 09:45-15:30 (seed 17)
data.windows: mbp-10 from signal - 120 s to signal + 300 s for each signal
data.tape: outcomes priced from the SIP tape as in the 10/3 studies (exec_report.nbbo_at; tools/tape_check.regular_prints), never from paper fills

features_at_signal.OBI5: (sum of bid sizes at the top 5 Nasdaq levels - sum of ask sizes) / (their total), from the last mbp-10 update at or before the signal
features_at_signal.ASK_THIN30: ask depth over the top 5 levels at the signal / its mean over the 30 s before, minus 1 (negative = asks draining)
features_at_signal.note: features use only book updates at or before the signal (no look-ahead); Nasdaq's book only, not consolidated

outcome.market_net: buy at the SIP ask at the signal, sell at the SIP bid after H, H in {60 s, 300 s, the desk trade's own hold}; bp
outcome.primary_horizon: the desk trade's own hold (what the desk would actually earn)

split: by date: first half / second half of the sample days
procedure: cut-offs are fixed on the FIRST half only (OBI5 top tercile; ASK_THIN30 bottom tercile) and applied unchanged to the second half

hypotheses.H1_PRIMARY: OBI5 gate: desk signals in the first-half-fixed top OBI5 tercile have higher market_net (primary horizon) than the rest
hypotheses.H2: ASK_THIN30 gate: desk signals in the bottom tercile (asks draining) have higher market_net than the rest
hypotheses.H3_info: the same on random entries (does depth pick direction without the desk's selection?); OBI1; 60 s and 300 s horizons

statistic: mean bp per signal, t clustered by day; gated-minus-rest difference and gated level
pass: H1 (or H2, reported separately, no pooling): in the SECOND half, gated desk signals beat the rest by >= +5 bp with day-clustered t >= 2, the gated signals' own market_net is > 0, and n >= 60 gated signals; the first half is only for fixing cut-offs. With two primary-ish gates, each must pass on its own (no best-of).
if_pass: result-skeptic review of the positive, then a firm quote for LIVE Nasdaq depth (exchange fees differ from historical), then a paper A/B with live depth — no live money on this result alone
if_fail: order-book depth is not worth buying for the desk's horizon; the paid-data question is closed
prior: low (~10-20%): book imbalance is known to predict seconds-scale mid moves usually smaller than the spread; the desk acts on 0.25-2 s ticks via IEX quotes and REST orders
caveats: the sample covers only recent sessions (since 9/16), so the second half is small
Nasdaq-listed subset of the desk's names
